hook: AI gave me a 47-step plan when I asked how to organize my closet. I have 12 shirts.
caption:
AI gave me a 47-step plan when I asked how to organize my closet. I have 12 shirts.

This is the thing nobody talks about.

AI doesn't know if you're a person who color-codes everything or someone who considers "floor pile" an organizational system.

It doesn't know if you want the Marie Kondo deep-dive or the "give me 3 things I can do in 20 minutes" version.

So it hedges. It gives you everything. It covers all the bases.

And you get a 47-step closet plan.

The BEFORE:
"Here's a comprehensive guide to wardrobe organization. Step 1: Remove all items. Step 2: Clean the space. Step 3: Categorize by type. Step 4: Subcategorize by color. Step 5: Consider seasonal rotation..."

The AFTER (once AI actually knows you're a Minimalist Executor type who wants fast and frictionless):
"Three moves. Trash bag for anything you haven't worn in 6 months. Everything else grouped by what you grab together. Done in 20 minutes."

Same question. Completely different answer.

The AI wasn't broken in the first version. It just didn't know you.

That's what bootfile.ai fixes. Your thinking style, your tolerance for detail, your version of "helpful" — all of it gets baked into how AI responds to you.

No more answers built for the average person.

You're not average.
